card.title: PS5 Power Rail, Standby Current, PMIC Pinout and Diagnostic Guide

claims.statement: If a PS5 is stuck at 7mA standby current, check the Dialog DA9065 PMIC voltages and the 25MHz and 32kHz Southbridge clock signals.
claims.evidence: Standby current chart indicates testing DA9065 output voltages and Southbridge crystal clocks when current remains at 7mA.
claims.quote: When console get’s standby power if it is stuck at 7mA. Check the voltages of Dialog ic and frequency of the 25Mhz clock and the 32Khz clock of the Southbridge IC.

claims.statement: Residual flux left under the Southbridge BGA can disrupt the 25MHz and 32kHz crystal oscillator signals.
claims.evidence: Source notes state that flux under the Southbridge BGA causes oscillator failure.
claims.quote: Flux under BGA can cause oscillator problems.

claims.statement: A firmware update error reading 'Can’t perform this action. Multiple USB drives are connected' indicates an unfixable APU defect.
claims.evidence: USB data lines route directly to the APU, making this update error a directly diagnosed APU failure.
claims.quote: If the error message is: Can’t perform this action. Multiple USB drives are connected APU is faulty and not fixable

claims.statement: To test SSD circuit current draw, measure across the pads of fuse F7520 in series using a multimeter in current mode; healthy draw is 310mA.
claims.evidence: Removing fuse F7520 isolates the SSD power regulator for direct current measurement.
claims.quote: Remove fuse F7520 that feeds the voltage on the back to the voltage regulator that generates power for the SSD circuit. Set a multimeter in current mode in series with the pads of the fuse and measure the current draw. G

claims.statement: The RAM +1.35V switching regulator line has a normal impedance of approximately 40 Ohms.
claims.evidence: Diagram specifies 40 Ohms impedance on the RAM power rail.

claims.statement: If the PS5 beeps 3 times upon pressing power but does not turn on while all rail voltages are normal, suspect BIOS firmware corruption.
claims.evidence: Flowchart and diagnosis guide associate 3 beeps with intact voltages but corrupt BIOS.
claims.quote: When console beep 3 times but not powers on check all voltages if all ok it could be a BIOS corruption.

procedure: {'step': 'Remove fuse F7520 on the back of the board feeding voltage to the SSD regulator.'}
{'step': 'Set a multimeter to current measurement mode.'}
{'step': 'Place the multimeter probes in series across the pads of fuse F7520.'}
{'step': 'Measure standby current draw and compare against the expected 310mA reading.'}
{'step': 'If current draw differs significantly, replace the SSD controller IC.'}

cautions: SOURCE RISK: A bench lab power supply used to run a PS5 must be capable of supplying at least 30 Amps at +12V during startup.
Flux under BGA components can compromise crystal oscillator frequency operation.
card.caveats: Ensure board state (standby vs power-on) matches the rail diagram context when taking diode and voltage measurements.
